prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: In an oral history recorded decades later, one fellow trustee called her the board's ______ during those years.

worlds.passage: For most of the 1960s a retired surgeon sat on the nine-member board of trustees of a county hospital. The board's rules allowed only its finance committee to place a spending request on the agenda, and she chaired that committee for the whole decade. Department heads seeking a new ward or a costly machine sent their requests to the committee, which met in her office; of the forty or so requests that arrived each year, about five reached the full board, and the trustees approved nearly every one they saw. In an oral history recorded decades later, one fellow trustee called her the board's ______ during those years.
worlds.explanation: Only her committee could put spending on the agenda, and only about five of forty requests a year got past it to a board that approved almost all it saw, so she controlled what reached the board: its "gatekeeper." "Figurehead" fails because that control was real power, not a title without it. "Envoy" fails because her work was screening requests coming in, not representing the board to anyone outside it. "Holdout" fails because she was not resisting a decision the other trustees had reached.

figurehead.quote: about five reached the full board
figurehead.why: her committee decided which requests the board ever saw, which is real power, the opposite of an empty title

envoy.quote: sent their requests to the committee
envoy.why: the traffic runs from department heads in to her; she carries nothing out to outside parties

holdout.quote: the trustees approved nearly every one they saw
holdout.why: the board agreed with what she sent; there is no majority she refused to join

worlds.passage: For most of the 1960s a retired surgeon sat on the nine-member board of trustees of a county hospital. She was the board's chair for the whole decade, and her name headed its letterhead. The bylaws gave the chair no vote except to break a tie, and the agenda and the budget were drawn up each year by the hospital's administrator, whose recommendations the other eight trustees adopted at nearly every meeting; in ten years no vote ever ended in a tie. In an oral history recorded decades later, one fellow trustee called her the board's ______ during those years.
worlds.explanation: She held the top title, but her only vote was a tie-breaker that was never needed and the administrator set the agenda the others followed, so she was the board's "figurehead": its nominal head without power. "Gatekeeper" fails because the administrator, not she, decided what came before the board. "Envoy" fails because nothing she did carried the board's business to outsiders. "Holdout" fails because she never cast a vote at all, let alone one against the majority.

gatekeeper.quote: drawn up each year by the hospital's administrator
gatekeeper.why: someone else controlled what reached the board, so she controlled no access

envoy.why: her role was a name and a chair inside the board; no mission to outside parties is described

holdout.quote: no vote ever ended in a tie
holdout.why: her only vote was a tie-breaker that never arose, so she could not have stood against the others

worlds.passage: For most of the 1960s a retired surgeon sat on the nine-member board of trustees of a county hospital. The hospital depended on a yearly grant from the state health department and on a road the county commissioners maintained to its door. Each spring for the whole decade, the trustees settled in closed session on what to ask of both, and she traveled to the capital and the county seat to present those requests and returned with the officials' terms for the board to debate. In an oral history recorded decades later, one fellow trustee called her the board's ______ during those years.
worlds.explanation: The board decided its requests together and she carried them to state and county officials and brought their terms back, so she was its "envoy," its representative sent to outside parties. "Gatekeeper" fails because she did not decide what the board considered; the trustees settled the requests and debated the terms. "Figurehead" fails because negotiating with officials was real work, not a title. "Holdout" fails because she carried a position the trustees shared rather than resisting it.

gatekeeper.quote: the trustees settled in closed session
gatekeeper.why: the whole board chose what to request and debated what came back; she screened nothing

figurehead.why: she did the substantive bargaining herself, which an empty title does not do

holdout.why: she presented the board's own agreed requests, so she was not refusing to join the others

worlds.passage: For most of the 1960s a retired surgeon sat on the nine-member board of trustees of a county hospital. In 1962 the state offered to fund a merger of the hospital with a larger one in the next county, on condition that the board approve it unanimously. The other eight trustees voted for the merger that year and at each of the four annual votes that followed, while she voted against it every time, arguing that the county's farm towns would lose their only emergency room; the offer expired in 1967. In an oral history recorded decades later, one fellow trustee called her the board's ______ during those years.
worlds.explanation: The merger needed every vote, eight trustees gave theirs five years running, and she alone refused until the offer lapsed, so she was the board's "holdout." "Gatekeeper" fails because she did not screen what reached the board; the merger came before it every year. "Figurehead" fails because her single vote decided the outcome. "Envoy" fails because she did not represent the board to the state; she opposed the board's own majority.

gatekeeper.quote: at each of the four annual votes
gatekeeper.why: the proposal reached the board every year; she controlled no access to it, she voted on it

figurehead.quote: on condition that the board approve it unanimously
figurehead.why: under that condition her lone vote decided the matter, which is real power

envoy.quote: she voted against it every time
envoy.why: she acted against the board's majority, not on its behalf toward outsiders
